messages:
anya: Quick sync 14AC Need final hero copy for the three product pages (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private). Can we settle on concise headlines + supporting lines? Aim: clarity for engineers and infra buyers.

mike: pinged. Can someone paste the live copy so I don't guess?

anya: Live (short):
```
Hosted API
Headline: Use our API to add LLM features
Subhead: Curated models, fast onboarding, auto-scale.

Dedicated
Headline: Reserved GPU capacity for your apps
Subhead: Predictable throughput and enterprise controls.

Private
Headline: Run inference in your environment
Subhead: On-prem or VPC with full compliance support.
```

kim: Thanks. Two quick priorities: 1) be explicit about cost so non-technical buyers know we reduce surprises; 2) keep verbs active.

sophia: Suggestion: Hosteds should foreground developer speed; Dedicated should foreground predictable SLAs; Private should foreground security/control.

jared: For SEO we should include keywords on meta tags not in visible hero. But squeeze in one short phrase in subhead if it reads naturally, e.g., "— low-latency inference" as a trailing fragment (we can hide in aria if needed).

mike: Draft A (concise, product-led):
```
Hosted API
Headline: Build LLM features fast
Subhead: Instant API, scale on demand, predictable per-token cost.
CTA primary: Get started
CTA secondary: See performance benchmarks

Dedicated
Headline: Reserved GPU capacity, guaranteed throughput
Subhead: SLA-backed pools, autoscale policies, enterprise isolation.
CTA primary: Request capacity
CTA secondary: View SLA details

Private
Headline: Run inference inside your network
Subhead: On-prem or VPC deployment with KMS and audit logging.
CTA primary: Contact sales
CTA secondary: Deployment options
```

anya: Solid. A couple edits: Hosted subhead "predictable per-token cost" is good. For Dedicated, change "Request capacity" -> "Request dedicated capacity" to improve clarity for sales routing. Private primary CTA should be "Request private deployment" so support team gets the right form.

olivia: For the A/B test, let's experiment with a second variant that leads with outcomes vs actions. Variant B language idea: Hosted: "Ship features 2x faster"; Dedicated: "Keep latency consistent at scale"; Private: "Meet compliance and keep data onsite." We'll measure signup rate and demo request rate. UTM: hero.copy.v2

sophia: Meta titles I'm drafting will include target keywords: Hosted: "Hosted API 1low-latency inference | Redwood Inference" (I'll polish). Also adding OG descriptions so social shares look good.

jared: Shared a short keyword matrix in Drive. Targets: "low-latency inference", "dedicated gpu inference", "private LLM deployment". Recommend meta descriptions include those phrases once.

anya: Ops question: do we want the hero to mention pricing model (usage-based) for Hosted? Might be distracting.

kim: Keep hero focused. Add a small badge below hero for "Usage-based pricing" linking to pricing page. That satisfies transparency without clutter.

marketing-bot: Created branch: copy/hero-three-updates-197260 1 PR: https://git.redwood.ai/copy/compare/copy/hero-three-updates-197260 1 reviewers: anya, mike, sophia 1 status: open

mike: I'll push both variants into the staging templates and include the CTAs we decided. ETA 3 hours.

olivia: Optimizely setup: event names hero_primary_click, hero_secondary_click, demo_request. Added audience = new visitors 0-30 days. Starting test tomorrow 06:00 UTC.

sophia: Meta titles/descriptions uploaded to PR. Example Hosted meta: "Hosted API 1 Instant API access to low-latency inference with predictable per-token costs. Try Redwood Hosted."

jared: Confirmed with SEO that trailing phrase in subheads shouldn't hurt readability. We'll prefer meta placement where possible.

anya: Action summary:
- Mike: push variants A/B to staging with CTAs (3h).
- Sophia: finalize meta titles/descriptions in PR (today EOD).
- Olivia: launch Optimizely test (tomorrow 06:00 UTC).
- Jared: confirm keyword placement and final SEO doc.
- Kim: add pricing badge copy and link.
- Marketing-bot: tag PR reviewers and merge when approved.
